items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee mentions Bob Shaw only in the context of describing a show produced by Billy Rose, stating 'the chorale was under the conduction of Shaw... Bob Shaw I guess his name is.' There is no indication of a personal or professional relationship between Teddy Wilson and Bob Shaw.

ctx.x: William Shuman who was then on the way to becoming the new young President of Juilliard, and now he's President of Lincoln Center.

And the chorale, the music, the popular music of the show was composed by Cole Porter, the chorale was under the conduction of Shaw, that famous choral conductor -- Bob Shaw I guess his name is. And he conducted the chorus in a gorgeous arrangement of 'Every Time We Say Goodbye,' acapella thing. So the show -- and Goodman's Quintet playing jazz. Billy Rose really loved music, and he surrounded himself with some of the best music that you could have at that time. All put together, it didn't mesh or blend as a…
